import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_88/test_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_88/test_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_88/test_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_88/test_3.csv"
]

# List to hold DataFrames from each source
dfs = []

# Load each source CSV, ignoring the first column as index (index_col=0)
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    dfs.append(df)

# All source tables have the same schema and the target schema is a subset (only 'TrackID')
# According to Hint 2 and Hint 4, we can UNION all source tables first, then select the 'TrackID' column.
# This will gather all TrackID values from all sources.

# Concatenate all source DataFrames (union)
combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Select only the 'TrackID' column as per target schema
target_df = combined_df[['TrackID']]

# Remove duplicate TrackID rows if any (to match target examples which show unique TrackID values)
# The target examples show unique TrackID values, so we keep unique TrackIDs only.
target_df = target_df.drop_duplicates().reset_index(drop=True)

# Ensure TrackID is integer type as per target schema
target_df['TrackID'] = target_df['TrackID'].astype(int)

# Write the result to the specified output path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_88/target_multisource_cot.csv"
target_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
